readout: qubit mode 9.28 GHz · Q ≈ 3,500 · 99.6 % of its inductive energy in the junction · anharmonicity ≈ 670 MHz
caption: A Palace eigenmode simulation of the first-generation SQUAT (the device of Magoon et al.) on sapphire, with the junction as a 10.2 nH inductor (EJ/h ≈ 16 GHz): about 550,000 tetrahedra. Shown is the unstructured mesh where it cuts a plane 0.25 µm above the metal, and the electric-field energy of the qubit's mode (logarithmic colour). The mode sits across the gap between the two islands and along their edges, and leaks a little into the feedline. Palace finds it at 9.28 GHz, with Q ≈ 3,500 from the feedline, 99.6 % of its inductive energy in the junction and an anharmonicity of about 670 MHz, in line with these devices' 8.8–9.3 GHz design (the measured ones came out at 7.4–8.5 GHz). The next modes, of the box and the feedline, are above 48 GHz. The junction is drawn schematically, so these are model values. Hover to read values.
